subject: gov.policy
name: Government Cloud Policy (data sovereignty and classification)
milestone: Draft issued 29 June 2023, unsigned
position_start: Draft, not enacted (2025-08)
position_end: Sets a draft data-sovereignty and data-classification rule for government workloads and has not been signed into effect; it is the nearest thing The Gambia holds to a localisation instrument

subject: gov.policy
name: Government Cloud Strategy 2023-2027
milestone: Issued 23 June 2023
position_start: In force (2025-08)
position_end: The consultant-authored strategy finds the Tier-2 government data centre power-constrained and reliant on diesel backup, which is the condition any migration has to work around

subject: gov.policy
name: Government e-interoperability framework
milestone: Proposed in the E-Government Strategy 2021-2024
position_start: Proposed, nothing built (2025-08)
position_end: The e-government strategy proposes an interoperability framework and an ICT agency; the agency exists and the framework does not, and no interoperability layer is recorded as operating

subject: gov.policy
name: Government Open Data Strategy 2024-2027
milestone: Adopted for 2024-2027
position_start: Adopted, targets unmet (2025-08)
position_end: The strategy records that The Gambia has no data registry, no open-data legal framework and no portal, and sets targets for 2026

subject: gov.policy
name: ICT for Development Policy Statement 2018-2028
status: Discontinued, superseded by the National Digital Economy Master Plan
milestone: Issued December 2017
position_start: Superseded (2025-08)
position_end: The foundational eight-pillar ICT policy, overtaken by the 2024-2034 master plan while its own stated period still runs to 2028

subject: gov.policy
name: National Broadband Policy and Strategy 2020-2024
status: Discontinued, the term expired with no successor located
milestone: Term ended 2024
position_start: Expired (2025-08)
position_end: The costed plan set 5 Mbps for all, 90 per cent coverage and 85 per cent 4G by 2024; the term has ended and no successor broadband instrument was located

subject: gov.policy
name: National Cybersecurity Strategy and Action Plan 2022-2026
milestone: Revised edition published, superseding the Proposed Formulation and Action Plan of July 2016
position_start: In force, on a period running to 2026 (2025-08)
position_end: Unchanged; no successor, mid-term review or implementation report is held, and the plan runs out at the end of 2026 (2026-08)
note: Four pillars: legal and regulatory strengthening, identification of critical information infrastructure, child online safety, and compliance with international cybersecurity standards and treaties. Its training and awareness uptake target was dated by 2023

subject: gov.policy
name: National Data Policy 2025
milestone: Draft published by the communications ministry
position_start: Draft, not adopted (2025-08)
position_end: Still a draft; no adoption, gazetting or implementation instrument is held (2026-08)

subject: gov.policy
name: National Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034
milestone: Adopted for the period 2024 to 2034
position_start: In force as the framing instrument for the digital programme (2025-08)
position_end: Unchanged; no mid-term review, monitoring report or costed implementation plan is held (2026-08)
sources: 2024-01-01 Gambia National Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034

subject: gov.policy
name: National Digital Identity Strategy 2023-2028
milestone: Validated at a UN Economic Commission for Africa-supported workshop, 17 May 2024
position_start: In force, with the identity system it provides for not yet built (2025-08)
position_end: In force and now carrying a delivered identity system (2026-07)
sources: 2024-05-17 Validation of The Gambia's National Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy|2024-01-01 Gambia National Digital Identity Strategy (Strategy Report)

subject: gov.policy
name: Science, technology and innovation policy 2027-2035
milestone: Validated 2026-08-31
position_start: a previous policy its own minister concedes achieved none of its objectives
position_end: a validated ten-year successor policy

subject: gov.legislate
name: Access to Information Act
milestone: Press union reported implementation ineffective 2026-08-07
position_end: In force, but with most public institutions yet to appoint the information officers the Act requires and twenty-one-day requests going unanswered
note: the account of non-implementation is the press union's; no government response, compliance count or enforcement action is on record

subject: gov.legislate
name: Artificial intelligence legislation or regulation
status: Not held, searched 2026-09-04 - no instrument located and the policy is still in drafting
milestone: No instrument found
position_start: No AI instrument (2025-08)
position_end: Still none: the ministry told the United Nations science and technology commission in April 2026 that a national artificial intelligence policy remains in development, and no bill, regulation or guideline has been laid

subject: gov.legislate
name: Broadcasting and Online Content Regulations, 2026
milestone: Draft issued for public consultation 2026-04-02; child-protection provisions set out by the information minister 2026-08-16
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A draft instrument made by the minister in charge of broadcasting content under section 226(1) of the Information and Communications Act (Cap. 74:03) in consultation with the regulator, issued for public consultation on 2 April 2026 as one of seven draft instruments released together — among them Journalists Registration Guidelines, 2026 and licensing, registration and authorisation guidelines. Its fourteen parts run from objectives and general obligations through a content complaints committee, licensing and professional standards, classification tiers, content monitoring, local-content promotion, coverage of public events, public service broadcasting, watershed and children's programming, complaints handling, and enforcement and sanctions; the child-protection provisions the information minister set out cover the identity of child victims, parental or guardian consent for interviews with children, and content that harms or exploits minors
note: a draft: its execution block is unsigned and undated, and it is dated here from the regulator's own consultation notice; no consultation closing date or adoption date is published

subject: gov.legislate
name: Communications Bill 2025
milestone: Sitting with National Assembly committees after second reading on 2 March 2026
position_start: Not introduced; first reading followed on 19 November 2025 (2025-08)
position_end: Passed second reading and referred to committee, with the Press Union pressing for repeal of the restrictive media laws around it (2026-07)
note: The Bill covers electronic communications, broadcasting, electronic commerce, electronic signatures, computer misuse and cybercrime in one instrument.

subject: gov.legislate
name: Gambia ICT Agency Act 2019
milestone: Agency constituted under the 2019 Act
position_start: In force (2025-08)
position_end: Gives the agency powers over a government data bank, technical standards, electronic signatures and cloud services - the statutory hooks an interoperability framework would hang on, none of them yet exercised in a published instrument

subject: gov.legislate
name: Information and Communications Act 2009
milestone: Assented 29 May 2009
position_start: In force (2025-08)
position_end: Carries The Gambia's computer-misuse, cybercrime and data-processing provisions; the Communications Bill 2025 that would replace it is still in committee

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Research, Development and Innovation Council Bill
milestone: Approved by cabinet 2026-08-29
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: a bill approved by cabinet to establish a national research, development and innovation council

subject: gov.legislate
name: Regulation for the Provision of Mobile Money Services 2011
milestone: Made 15 October 2011
position_start: In force (2025-08)
position_end: The central bank's mobile-money rulebook, setting a GMD10m capital floor, a cash-merchant regime and an interoperability duty; the instant payment switch launched in December 2025 is the duty's first delivery

subject: gov.legislate
name: State Intelligence Service Bill
milestone: Draft validated at a stakeholder workshop, 31 July 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Draft validated, reported to require judicial warrants and oversight for intrusive measures and to give the Assembly review of the Service's budgets and operations; not tabled (2026-07)
note: The text is not held and the Bill does not appear in the National Assembly's bills library, checked 2026-08-08; the provisions are as reported from the workshop.

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistics Act 2005
milestone: Reform urged by African Union peer review, November 2025
position_start: In force, revision recommended by the statistics strategy (2023-09)
position_end: Still unamended: the national statistical strategy found more than a third of officials unaware of the Act and called for its revision, and the African Union peer review of November 2025 urged mandate reform and a modernised statistics law
note: The 2005 Act is held only as an image-only scan with no machine-readable text.

subject: gov.protect
name: Data Protection and Privacy Commission
note: A commencement instrument, an appointment notice, a budget line or a first annual report. The Act provides for an independent Commission; nothing held states whether it has been constituted.

subject: gov.protect
name: Information Commission
milestone: Communication-strategy support agreed 2026-08-17
position_start: Not held
position_end: Operating as the body responsible for the Access to Information Act 2021 and the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2025, and receiving UNFPA-funded support under the Peacebuilding Fund's Public Accountability Project to build a communication strategy raising public awareness of both statutes
note: no budget, staffing, caseload or enforcement record for the commission is held, and awareness-raising support is not evidence of enforcement capacity

subject: gov.protect
name: Legal basis for issuing identity cards outside the country
note: An official response, a regulation or a registry statement covering issuance in Mauritania, Congo and Togo, which the opposition alleged was unlawful in August 2025.

subject: gov.protect
name: Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2025
milestone: Enacted, ending a legislative process stalled for several years
position_start: No comprehensive data-protection law; the Bill was before the National Assembly (2025-08)
position_end: Enacted, with extraterritorial scope, seven lawful bases, a sensitive-data regime covering genetic, biometric and health data, and rights of access, rectification, erasure and protection from solely automated decisions (2025-12)

subject: gov.regional
name: African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection
milestone: Signed 2 December 2022
position_start: Signed, ratification owed (2025-08)
position_end: The ministry's own record of signature on 2 December 2022 states ratification is still owed, and no instrument of ratification has been published since

subject: gov.regional
name: ATAF Heads of Tax Administrations Master Class
milestone: Seventh Master Class convened in Banjul, 23-24 July 2026
position_start: Did not exist as a Gambian commitment
position_end: Convened by the Gambia Revenue Authority, with the Forum's executive secretary arguing that digital systems deliver only alongside governance reform and pressing for a united African position in the United Nations tax convention negotiations (2026-07)

subject: gov.regional
name: Senegal-Gambia regulatory cooperation and free roaming agreement
milestone: Signed between the two regulators, June 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Signed, covering telecommunications regulatory cooperation and free roaming; no commencement date or tariff published (2026-06)

subject: gov.regional
name: Senegal–Gambia digital cooperation memorandum
milestone: First steering-committee session, Banjul, 29 August 2026
position_start: A memorandum signed at the fourth Senegalo-Gambian Presidential Council in June 2026, with no work agreed under it
position_end: The memorandum signed at Dakar on 12 June 2026 took its first steering-committee session at Banjul on 29 August 2026, settling four priorities - infrastructure and interoperability, cyber resilience, capacity building and regulatory harmonisation - with rural electronic-government access named among the work
note: no timetable, budget or named deliverable is attached to any of the four priorities

subject: gov.standards
name: The Gambia Standards Bureau
milestone: Correspondent member of ISO and IEC
position_start: Publishing a national standards catalogue, thin on ICT (2022-01)
position_end: Around 500 standards adopted and membership of the African standards organisation, against Correspondent non-voting status at ISO and IEC and the role of the country's technical-barriers enquiry point

subject: gov.discourse
name: Public participation in digital policymaking
milestone: Eight draft instruments opened for comment, 2 April 2026
position_start: No published consultation practice on digital policy (2025-08)
position_end: The utilities regulator opened public comment on eight draft instruments in April 2026 under published consultation guidelines, having validated ex-ante telecom pricing tools with stakeholders in November 2025; the national policy handbook mandates participatory, evidence-based policymaking, and a draft e-commerce policy was validated with public and private participants in September 2025
note: A consultation register, a published submission round, or a civil-society account of participation in the data, communications or intelligence bills.

subject: finance.budget
name: Domestic budget appropriations for the digital sector
note: An appropriation act, budget speech or estimate showing the votes for the communications ministry, the regulator and the digital programme.

milestone: Stated by the finance minister at the Banjul Master Class, 23 July 2026

subject: finance.budget
name: Total tax collected
milestone: Revenue authority 2026 target published, 3 August 2026
position_end: D25bn (2025), against a D27.5bn target for 2026
note: Carried in dalasi as the authority states it; the finance minister attributes the rise to digitalisation of collection rather than to rate increases, which is an attribution and not an evaluation.

subject: finance.mou
name: India-Gambia digital public infrastructure memorandum
milestone: Signed October 2024
position_start: Signed, no delivery recorded (2025-08)
position_end: India's own country brief records the memorandum signed in October 2024 with no funding figure and no milestones stated; the visible delivery is training rather than infrastructure

subject: finance.new
name: AfDB digital government project
milestone: Carried in the bank's own reporting as a pipeline operation
position_start: Pipeline (2025-08)
position_end: Still pipeline; no approval, signature or first disbursement is held (2026-08)
note: XDR 1,000,000, about US$1m, covering Sierra Leone and The Gambia jointly.

name: Gates Foundation payment system pilot
milestone: Recorded as closed in the funder's own reporting
position_start: Closed (2025-08)

milestone: US$50m equivalent grant approved, 7 November 2023
position_start: In implementation; no disbursement or results figure published (2025-08)
position_end: Unchanged; no disbursement, results framework or mid-term review is held (2026-08)
note: SDR 38.1m, stated as US$50.0m equivalent at approval, inside a US$293m regional operation with Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Mauritania, ECOWAS, the African Union and Smart Africa.

subject: infra.connect
name: Gambia National Broadband Network (China Eximbank loan)
milestone: Arrears of US$0.25m cleared, 19 June 2020
position_start: In service under a US$25.9m concessional loan repayable by GAMTEL, with a servicing history of arrears (2017 loan)
position_end: Unchanged on the record; no statement of network condition, utilisation or debt position since 2020
note: The loan is collateralised against a minimum escrow balance accessible to the lender.

subject: infra.connect
name: GAMTEL national broadband modernisation PPP
milestone: US$50m partnership signed at Bijilo, announced 5 January 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: US$50m partnership signed to take the national backbone from 40 Gbps to 800 Gbps; no completion date, milestone schedule or dalasi figure published (2026-01)
note: The US$50m is the figure as announced; no dalasi original is established.

subject: infra.connect
name: International capacity on the ACE submarine cable
milestone: Modernisation agreement signed 24 December 2025
position_start: 15 Gbps of international capacity through the state incumbent, which holds 49 per cent of the country's cable segment (2025-03)
position_end: A US$50m public-private partnership signed in December 2025 is to lift the national backbone from 40 to 800 Gbps; a second submarine cable is at bid evaluation across five states and the agreement was still unsigned in July 2026

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet use
milestone: Kepios estimate, October 2025
movement: No change, a first estimate with no comparable earlier figure
position_start: No national internet-use figure published by the statistics office
position_end: 1.30m internet users, 45.9 per cent of the population, against 3.19m mobile connections; the statistics office's own 2024 communication statistics publish 3.48m mobile subscribers and no internet penetration figure at all

subject: infra.connect

milestone: Signed by the three administrations, February 2025
position_start: Signed; no tariff, traffic or commencement figure published (2025-08)
position_end: Unchanged; no tariff, traffic or commencement figure published (2026-08)

subject: infra.connect
name: Serekunda Internet Exchange Point
milestone: Founded 25 July 2013 by 14 members
position_start: Operating, no traffic figures published (2025-08)
position_end: The country's only exchange point, founded in 2013 by fourteen members, still publishing no current traffic or member figures

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink satellite service licence
milestone: Minister of Digital Economy stated he had refused to approve the permit, 24 May 2026
position_start: Fee paid and licence unissued for over a year, the government citing due diligence in the face of United States pressure (2025-07)
position_end: Still unlicensed; the minister states Starlink lacks the competencies and equipment for a VSAT permit and requires a general satellite licence instead (2026-05)
note: The base carries a fee paid in December 2024 and a permit payment in February 2026; whether these are the same payment is not established.

subject: infra.store
name: National Data Centre, Abuko

subject: infra.energy

milestone: Solar park reported in service, February 2025
position_end: 23 MWp of solar with 8 MWh of battery storage, one of two parks totalling 48 MWp built under a combined US$149m investment providing new or improved electricity to 500,000 people across two countries
note: the beneficiary figure is the two countries combined; no Gambia-only count is stated, and no source ties the generation to the digital estate

subject: infra.energy
name: Power supply to the national digital estate
milestone: Utility admits long-term load shedding, April 2026
position_start: A Tier-2 government data centre found power-constrained and reliant on diesel backup (2023-06)
position_end: The utility admitted a 26 MW deficit and long-term feeder shedding in April 2026, then restored two generators in June 2026 with a 50 MW solar contract days from signature; national electricity access stood at 73.7 per cent in 2024
note: A generation, tariff or outage statement bearing on data-centre or network operation, or the power provision in either data centre's design.

subject: infra.energy
name: Rural electricity access programme
milestone: US$160m regional financing approved 24 June 2026
position_start: 73.7 per cent electricity access in 2024, against a compact target of 100 per cent by 2030 (2025-01)
position_end: A 719-community switch-on tour ran in February 2026 and the World Bank approved US$160m of financing for electricity access in Togo and The Gambia in June 2026, against a utility admitting a 26 MW deficit and long-term load shedding

subject: infra.capacity
name: Domestic technical capacity to operate the national digital systems
milestone: Incident response team trained by the ITU, May 2026
position_start: No published account of domestic capacity to run the national systems (2025-08)
position_end: The incident response team was trained on ticketing, threat-sharing and open-source intelligence tooling over two weeks in May 2026 under a programme funded by the regional digital project, and a certified two-week course in results-based management and data analytics for officials opened in July 2026
note: A staffing plan, skills audit or operations report covering who runs the National Data Centre, the identity system and the payment switch.

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National cybersecurity agency or incident response team
status: Planned, no evidence of operation held
milestone: GM-CSIRT named as the national incident response team in the National Cybersecurity Strategy and Action Plan 2022-2026
position_start: No position held at the start of the window
position_end: An institutional design on paper: GM-CSIRT operating a national Cybersecurity Centre with a security operations centre inside it, a National Cybersecurity Coordination Directorate, a National Cybersecurity Commission, an advisory board, sectoral focal points and sector CSIRTs, and a police cybercrime response unit. The plan directs that GM-CSIRT be operationalised and strengthened in budget and technology; nothing held states that any of these bodies is standing
note: The strategy is a design document, not a capability statement; no incident report, budget line or annual report naming any of these bodies is held

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Gambia-Senegal customs data exchange roadmap
milestone: Three-month roadmap agreed at the second Monitoring Committee, Saly, 16-17 July 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Agreed to install the GAINDE customs system at Karang, Keur Ayib and Selety within three months, deploy SIGMAT transit tracking, exchange customs data by interface once GAINDE is live, replace transit agents with a Single Administrative Document and reactivate the EnCen intelligence platform (2026-07)

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Interoperability between the social, civil and education registers
milestone: One link under verification, November 2025
position_start: No register linked to another (2025-08)
position_end: The project indicator for interoperability between the social registry, the education system, civil registration and health insurance stands at zero with one link being verified

position_end: Launched for criminal investigations with European Union and international police support; no cost figure is published and the delegation's statement of its legal basis is uncited

subject: dpi.id
name: Birth certificate to identity card to passport credential chain
milestone: Section 4A, Immigration Act CAP 16:02
position_start: In force (2025-08)
position_end: The government's own statement of how the credentials fit together: a birth certificate supports an identity card, which supports a passport, with a biometric passport fee of D5,100

subject: dpi.id
name: Margins ID national identity contract
milestone: Enrolment demand exceeding daily caps 2026-08-28
position_start: Did not exist; the standing arrangement was the concession the 2025 State of the Nation address set out to replace (2025-08)
position_end: enrolment running with high demand meeting daily processing caps at centres in the Greater Banjul Area, on field reporting

note: No contract value is published in anything held.

subject: dpi.id
name: National Identity Management System (GAM ID)
milestone: Phased rollout calendar and fee published, 2026-08-25
position_start: Did not exist; identity cards were produced under a foreign concession the government had resolved to replace (2025-08)
position_end: Live and issuing instant cards from the National Data Centre, with nationwide rollout of new ten-year biometric national identity cards launched on 7 August 2026. Phase-one registration for citizens aged eighteen and over began on 4 August 2026 at seven Greater Banjul centres, extending to Sibanor and Jarra Soma on 7 September, to Barra, Kerewan, Farafenni and Kaur on 11 September and to Janjanbureh, Basse and Fatoto on 21 September; the first-time card costs D450, waived during the rollout for holders of a valid immigration department card or enrolment printout
note: no enrolment or issuance figure has been published since launch; the cards are produced with a Ghana-based supplier. An applicant with no passport, birth certificate or prior identity document must be vouched for by both the Alkalo and the Seyfo of their place of residence

subject: dpi.id
name: Refugee identity cards and travel documents
milestone: Provided for by the Refugee Act 2008
position_start: Provided for in statute, no enrolment figures published (2025-08)
position_end: The 2008 Act constitutes the refugee commission and provides for refugee identity cards and travel documents; 4,214 refugees and 552 other people of concern were recorded at 31 May 2026, and no count of cards issued is published

subject: dpi.pay

position_end: First inclusive instant payment system in service, built on Mojaloop and operated by GamSwitch across banks, mobile money, microfinance institutions and fintechs; no transaction volume published (2025-12)

position_start: Did not exist

position_end: Unchanged; no deployment, route or volume figure published (2026-08)
